decision: Spike code lives on spike/ branches that are never merged; only the written records are merged
why: The brief says spike code is not product code, and S-6 needs steps the owner can re-run

decision: Fixed for the spikes: Python, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, one injectable clock, S3-compatible storage in production
why: Brief assumption 4; the v3 build proved this stack through daily reports; the spec's 3,599/3,600-second link boundary can only be tested if the application checks expiry with its own clock

decision: Kept the 31 Gherkin feature files verbatim under docs/spec/<area>/ and listed them under 尚未建置 in each area index, instead of rewriting 254 scenarios as prose
why: They are already Given/When/Then, the owner agreed their rules, and later tasks bind tests to these exact files; rewriting would risk changing meaning

decision: Renamed the two CFG-F02 scenarios both called "Validation"
why: Runners that bind scenarios by name silently drop one; v3 recorded this pitfall. Steps and examples are unchanged

decision: Corrected the scenario total from 251 to 254 and added a count of 502 cases
why: Counted by a Gherkin parser; v3's hand-kept table was stale for MAT-F03 and PAY-F01

decision: Added tools/check_spec.py and tools/requirements.txt as the only code merged by this task
why: S-3 needs a command that checks the spec; seen to fail on a wrong total, a duplicate scenario name and broken Gherkin

decision: Did not turn the open-question defaults into new scenarios in the baseline
why: The brief limits baseline changes to v3's own decisions; new behaviour should be approved by the owner in the brief of the task that builds it

decision: Added .gitignore for .claude/worktrees/, .venv/ and __pycache__/
why: Commit 39ae504 picked up two builder worktrees as embedded repositories through git add -A; removed in the next commit

decision: Chose a single server-rendered Python application on a dedicated PostgreSQL over a Supabase-centred shape and over the v2 two-tier shape
why: The spec's core rules are multi-table transactions with exact refusal messages; v2's two tiers caused three security defects

decision: Dropped v3's ban on database triggers and functions
why: That ban served a scanner needed only because v3 shared a database; immutability of audit rows and payroll runs is safer in the database

decision: Year-to-date retention is derived from confirmed shares, not accumulated from payroll runs
why: Re-running a period must not count retention twice; consistent with AD-3

decision: Payroll runs do not store bank numbers; the transfer slip decrypts at export time and cannot be produced without the key
why: Keeps plain bank numbers out of immutable rows; the spec is silent, so it is listed for the owner in the payroll task's brief

decision: Recommended Railway for the app and scheduler trigger, a dedicated Supabase project as plain PostgreSQL, and S3-compatible storage
why: The owner knows these; the application touches Supabase only through the connection string, so the choice is reversible by configuration

decision: Chose argon2id for password hashing instead of v3's standard-library scrypt
why: A maintained library with tunable parameters so tests can use cheap ones; v3's full-strength hashing made its suite slow

decision: Put ARC-F01 with the ledger in task 7 after payroll, and noted the ledger could be split out to run earlier
why: Archives need confirmed reports and a payroll summary; both features share the file storage work

decision: Open-question defaults follow v3's implemented "option A" where v3 had one
why: The text of v3 issue 35 could not be read from this session; its seven topics come from v3's M2 report

decision: Download links are signed and expired by the application with the injected clock; files are served through the application
why: The object store's presigned URLs expire on the store's own clock, which tests cannot set, and a local directory has no equivalent, so local and production would run different code. Cost: every download passes through the application

decision: Receipt type is decided by the file's leading bytes; declared content type and extension are ignored, and the file is served with the detected type
why: The sender controls the declared type and the name; a GIF renamed to .pdf must still be refused. Side effect: a PNG named .html is accepted and served as image/png

decision: 10 MB is taken as 10 x 1024 x 1024 = 10,485,760 bytes
why: The ticket gives no byte count; this is the common meaning for upload limits

decision: Bank numbers use AES-256-GCM from the cryptography library with our own stored format v1.<key id>.<data>, not Fernet/MultiFernet
why: Fernet stores no key id, writes the system time into the value and cannot bind a value to its account. Cost: about 30 lines of format code are ours to maintain

decision: The last four digits are obtained by decrypting; they are not stored separately, so showing them needs the key
why: The required behaviour is that viewing shows 無法讀取 when the key is missing, which a stored last-four would contradict; it also keeps one owner for the value and no plaintext at rest. Measured cost: about 2 ms for 850 accounts

decision: Editing a bank number is refused whenever the stored value cannot be read (wrong key or corrupted value too, not only a missing key), and for an account with no value yet when no key is configured
why: The spec only covers the missing key. A wrong key is usually a configuration mistake that can be undone; overwriting would destroy recoverable data. Consequence: a truly corrupted row needs an administrator action to clear. Needs the owner's confirmation in the open-questions list

decision: The spike keeps records in memory instead of PostgreSQL, and its warning and error wording other than the two quoted bank messages is a placeholder
why: Neither question depends on the database, and the exact wording belongs to the spec baseline. Left unproven: delete and rotation against real tables

decision: Proved "seen to fail" with a script that breaks 34 behaviours one at a time on a temporary copy and reruns the tests, kept on the spike branch
why: The code was written before the tests, so each test had to be shown able to fail; a script lets the verifier and the owner repeat that

decision: An automatic archive is "due" as a state computed from the clock and the archives already stored, not an event fired at 23:59
why: A late, repeated or missed trigger then gives the same result, and a test needs only the clock

decision: The duplicate guard is a partial unique index (kind, period_date) WHERE automatic with INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; the archive row and its content share one transaction
why: The database decides, so it holds for any number of processes; without it 20 of 20 runs produced two archives

decision: Recommended production trigger: a loop inside each application process, with a one-shot command kept as the alternative entry. This differs from the design draft (platform cron)
why: Same code locally and in production, differing only in TICK_SECONDS; a platform cron still needs the same catch-up and guard

decision: Assumed: catch-up runs from the last automatic archive of each kind forward and never refills an older gap; a fresh install creates only the latest due date
why: The spec text I was given does not say; refilling could recreate an archive a person deleted. Listed as an owner decision

decision: Assumed: a session is expired from the instant expires_at is reached (inclusive)
why: The ticket only says expired sessions need cleanup

decision: Left open, not answered by the spike: whether a caught-up archive should hold the state at catch-up time or at the original 23:59
why: Archive content is out of scope for the ticket; only a placeholder is stored

decision: Replaced the reference font approach: PDF uses reportlab with Noto Sans TC Regular (SIL OFL 1.1, 7.1 MB) committed inside the application, not the fonts-noto-cjk system package
why: reportlab 5.1.0 rejects the package's fonts ("postscript outlines are not supported"); the built-in CID font is not embedded and poppler could not show it

decision: Cut a static Regular (wght 400) instance out of Google's variable Noto Sans TC with fonttools and committed the result
why: reportlab cannot select a weight axis and rendered the variable font as Thin

decision: Word export keeps python-docx with 標楷體 requested as the East Asian font; the transfer-slip layout is invented
why: A .docx does not embed fonts, so the server needs none; the real bank sample is not available and must be matched later

decision: Negative amounts are shown with a minus sign and in red; a negative row is included in the transfer slip only to show the format
why: The ticket asks for distinguishable negatives in both files; what a negative net pay means for a bank transfer is a business rule left to the owner

decision: Seen to fail is recorded as a script (prove_fail.py) that breaks each behaviour and requires its test to fail, instead of a note saying I did it
why: The ticket's check asks for it per behaviour, and a reader can re-run it

decision: Did not try HTML-to-PDF (WeasyPrint) or filling a real bank .docx as a template; both are described as untried
why: reportlab already produces the table; no real bank file exists to fill

decision: Changed the production trigger from a platform cron (the design draft) to a loop inside each application process, keeping the one-shot command
why: T-02 showed both rest on the same database guard, and the loop keeps local and production on the same code with one setting; a platform cron can still be added by configuration

decision: The PDF font ships inside the application (Noto Sans TC Regular, SIL OFL 1.1, 7.1 MB) instead of a system font package
why: T-02 found reportlab cannot load the fonts-noto-cjk package that v1 relied on

decision: Merged T-01 and T-02 without a separate per-ticket verification, after re-running each spike from a clean checkout of its branch
why: Care level is 一般; the final verification covers S-6. T-01: 68 passed; T-02: 30 passed and both sample files written

decision: Left test_command empty in .shilaycow/config.yml
why: The only check so far is tools/check_spec.py; the skeleton task will set the real test command when a suite exists
